title: Code in more than one file

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the labels file here to see the labels it prints, and the emails file once you have written it.

tasks.title: Share the price code
tasks.description:
At the bottom of `src/money.js`, under `// Task 1`, write an export line that shares `formatPrice` and `salePrice` with other files. `twoDigits` only helps `formatPrice`, so it is not exported.

Check imports `src/money.js` from a file of its own, looks at what it exports, and calls `formatPrice` and `salePrice` to make sure they still work as before.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on export.
Under the Task 1 comment, write the word export and a pair of curly braces.
Inside the braces, name the two functions other files need, with a comma between them.
Run `node src/money.js`: it prints nothing, and that is right. The next task uses what you shared.
hints: You have seen this kind of line at the bottom of every file of this repo. Now you write one yourself.
An export line names, in curly braces, the things this file shares. Anything it does not name stays inside the file, and that is where `twoDigits` belongs.
The line is `export { formatPrice, salePrice }`, on a line of its own.

tasks.title: Use the shared price
tasks.description:
In `src/labels.js`, remove `labelPrice`, the old copy of the price code. Import `formatPrice` from `money.js` at the top of the file, and make `shelfLabel` use it, so that `shelfLabel({ name: 'Amber', grams: 200, priceCents: 1850 })` gives `'Amber, 200 g, 18.50 EUR'`.

Check calls `shelfLabel` with candles of its own. It also puts a `money.js` of its own beside your file, to make sure the price really comes from there and not from a copy.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on import and on the path.
At the top of `labels.js`, under the first comments, write an import line for `formatPrice`.
In `shelfLabel`, use `formatPrice` in place of `labelPrice`, then remove `labelPrice`.
Run `node src/labels.js`: the Amber label should end in 18.50 EUR.
hints: An import line names what it wants in curly braces, then where it comes from. The names must match the export line of `money.js` exactly.
`money.js` sits beside `labels.js` in the same folder, so its path starts with `./`, and it ends with the whole file name, `.js` included.
The line is `import { formatPrice } from './money.js'`, and `shelfLabel` then has `${formatPrice(candle.priceCents)}` where it had `labelPrice`.

tasks.title: A label for the sale
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3` in `src/labels.js`, make `saleLabel(candle, percent)` give the label of a candle on sale: its name and grams as on the shelf label, then the sale price, then how much is off. `saleLabel(fig, 20)` gives `'Fig, 350 g, 19.20 EUR, 20% off'`. Work the sale price out with `salePrice` from `money.js` and write it with `formatPrice`. Put `export` in front of the word `function`.

Check calls `saleLabel` with candles and percents of its own, makes sure the sale price comes from `money.js`, and reads your file for the `export` in front.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on the two ways to export.
Add `salePrice` to the import line at the top of `labels.js`.
Write the body of `saleLabel`, then put `export` in front of its first line.
Run `node src/labels.js`: the last line should show the Fig label on sale.
hints: Two things come from `money.js` now. One import line can bring in more than one name, with commas between them.
Work out the sale price first, with `salePrice(candle.priceCents, percent)`, then hand that number to `formatPrice`. The label ends with the percent and the words `% off`.

The first line reads `export function saleLabel(candle, percent) {`, and the body returns `` `${candle.name}, ${candle.grams} g, ${formatPrice(salePrice(candle.priceCents, percent))}, ${percent}% off` ``.

tasks.title: A line for the order email
tasks.description:
Write `src/emails.js` yourself, under its comment: an import line that brings in `formatPrice` from `money.js`, and a function `orderLine(candle, qty)` that other files can import. It gives one line of the email: how many, an `x`, the candle's name, a comma, and what they cost together, written with `formatPrice`. `orderLine({ name: 'Cedar', priceCents: 1800 }, 2)` gives `'2 x Cedar, 36.00 EUR'`.

Check imports `orderLine` from your file, calls it with candles and counts of its own, and puts a `money.js` of its own beside it to make sure the price comes from there.
nextSteps: Look at how `labels.js` imports and exports now.
Write `orderLine` from the word `function` to its closing brace, and export it.
Add a `console.log` of your own and run `node src/emails.js`.
hints: Nothing is given in this file: the import, the function and its export are all yours. `labels.js` has every piece you need, in another order.
What they cost together is the price of one candle times `qty`, in cents. Hand that number to `formatPrice`.

The file has `import { formatPrice } from './money.js'`, then `export function orderLine(candle, qty) {` with a body that returns `` `${qty} x ${candle.name}, ${formatPrice(candle.priceCents * qty)}` ``.
